description: A feature in a small Python package (shopcrm: tools for an online tea shop's nightly customer export, with validate, lookup, and stats commands, tests, and four commits of history): a `dedupe` command, specified exactly in docs/dedupe.md, that collapses the export to one row per person, where rows sharing a normalized email or phone number are one person directly or through other rows. The prompt gives the real size (about 400k rows) as context and asks for nothing about speed. The obvious implementation compares each row with the people found so far, often through the repository's own pairwise same_customer(), or keeps seen values in lists; it is quadratic and passes every small test. Indexing rows by normalized email and phone (union-find, graph search, or sorting by each key) is near-linear. Required: hidden hand-made and generated cases print the reference's rows (compared as parsed CSV); the fixture's own tests pass from the check's copies; and on generated exports of 25k rows and of 400k rows (the size the person gives) the command finishes with one row per person, its CPU time within 10 times the reference's plus 1 s at each size, and its growth in CPU time from 25k to 400k rows at most twice the reference's growth. CPU time is the kernel's accounting of every process in the sandbox: the command runs under a reaper that is the sandbox's first process and reaps whatever is left when it exits, so processes nobody waited for (multiprocessing forkserver workers) count too. The measurement runs in rounds of the reference and the agent's code at both sizes back to back; the median of up to three rounds decides growth, and an agent run is stopped at its CPU bound, a size failing on the second such stop. Measures: medians over the rounds of CPU seconds and their ratios to the reference, both growths, each round's growth ratio, peak memory, exact large-output match, the agent's own suite, tests added, reuse of the shared normalization, and commits. Agent code runs only in bubblewrap. Needs bubblewrap and python3 3.11+ at /usr/bin or /usr/local/bin; agent arms need no readable entries. See qualify/README.md.
prompt: Our storefront makes a new customer account for every guest checkout, so the nightly customer export is full of the same people over and over. Last night's file was about 400k rows. The newsletter service bills us per contact, so before the sync uploads the export we need it collapsed to one row per actual person. Could you add a `dedupe` command to shopcrm for that? Priya wrote down exactly how she decides who is the same person and what each row should hold, in docs/dedupe.md.
